text:
marta: Quick follow-up to the multi-region RFC — question about representation: should we keep a per-tenant residency flag (tenant.residency = 'eu'|'us'|'any') or instead map tenants to cluster tags and let the proxy resolve (cluster: eu-west-1 -> tag: EU_RESIDENT)?
chris: my gut: tags are more flexible for rollouts, can map many clusters to one tag. but overhead to maintain mapping service.
kevin: per-tenant flag is simpler for policy eval. easier to reason about in billing/contract docs. downside: when we add a new eu cluster you have to update tenant metadata or a migration job.
devon: if we do cluster tags, proxy needs a lookup that is fast (cache TTL small). else routing latency jumps. also need strong observability for mis-maps.
marta: good points. thinking of hybrid: tenant.metadata.residency_hint + cluster.tags. residency_hint is authoritative for compliance, tags are used for runtime affinity and capacity. fallback rules decide when hint can't be honored.
rachel: agree hybrid makes sense. we should define clear precedence: 1) tenant residency_hint (hard), 2) tenant preferred_region list (soft), 3) proxy cluster tag match, 4) global pool fallback.
chris: how do we enforce "hard"? block if request would be routed outside region? or allow with audit + manual approval?
kevin: legal teams will want hard block for some customers. implement a policy toggle per-tenant: residency_enforcement = strict|warn|none. default warn.
devon: implementation sketch for proxy routing: when request arrives, proxy extracts X-Residency-Hint header (if present) or looks up tenant metadata. then it fetches compatible cluster list from ClusterTagCache. pseudo: ```
// pseudo
hint = req.headers['X-Residency-Hint'] || TenantStore.get(tenant).residency_hint
candidates = ClusterTagCache.getClustersForTag(hint)
route = pickLowestLoad(candidates) || ClusterTagCache.getClustersForTag('any')
```
chris: what about KV cache locality? active/active means KV eviction/lease transfer complexity. if we honor hint but route some reads to remote cluster, we'll need prefix cache shadowing.
kevin: yeah, we need to ensure cache TTLs consider cross-region penalties. maybe add a per-tenant cache_policy that prefers local warmups and longer kv TTL for remote reads.
marta: ops questions: how do we detect when hint can't be honored vs when it's simply overloaded? need distinct metrics: residency_miss (no matching cluster), residency_overflow (matching cluster full).
rachel: add two metrics, both tagged by tenant and enforcement mode. residency_miss should trigger immediate operator alert for strict tenants. residency_overflow should create autoscale/burst events.
devon: rollout plan: start with a small cohort of opt-in tenants using residency_enforcement=warn. run for 2 weeks, collect misses/overflows, and simulate strict mode enforcement in dry-run.
sre-bot: cluster-tag-cache refresh succeeded (duration 120ms) — clusters: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1, us-west-2, us-east-1]. health: ok.
chris: edge-case: data-copying during tenant migration between regions. need a portal + migration job that idempotently copy state and verify checksums. also require a migration-shield flag to prevent dual-writes during cutover.
kevin: propose API for migration: POST /admin/tenants/:id/migrate {target_region, dry_run:true|false} returns job id. job steps: snapshot -> copy -> verify -> flip residency_hint -> drain old cluster.
marta: add a boolean "allow_cross_region_reads" that customers can set for eventual consistency use-cases. default false for compliance tenants.
rachel: docs: update SLA and security page to mention enforcement modes and what triggers alerts. also add clear guidance for contract/legal teams.
devon: ops-runbooks: add playbook for residency_miss for strict tenants: 1) identify cause (tag mismatch vs decomm), 2) temporary failover toggle (for emergencies only), 3) kick migration job.
chris: dev question: will SDKs expose X-Residency-Hint header by default? I think server-side clients should set it from tenant metadata; SDKs can optionally accept override for debugging.
marta: agreed — SDK heuristic: prefer automatic, allow opt-in header to force when caller has privilege. log overrides.
kevin: telemetry items: percent requests honoring hint, latency delta when honoring vs fallback, burst count per-tenant.
rachel: security: ensure header can't be spoofed for strict tenants — authenticate via signed header or proxy-enforced header set by auth layer.
devon: we also need migration of existing tenants without residency_hint. add discovery job that tags tenants with probable_region = top-request-origin 30d. but mark as inferred and only used for soft preferences.
marta: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with enforcement modes, precedence table, metrics, and migration API. tag @legal to review strict enforcement wording.
chris: looks good, +1 to hybrid approach.
kevin: +1. i'll sketch migration API details tomorrow.
rachel: i'll draft the docs changes after the RFC addendum.
sre-bot: reminder: weekly oncall handover at 17:00 UTC.
